key_insight: Supersonic turbulent shear layers become self-similar far downstream, and that self-similar behavior can be captured across different compressibility and velocity-parameter conditions with appropriate scaling.
engineering_relevance: The results provide practical scaling laws and entrainment predictions for designing and modeling high-speed mixing layers in propulsion, combustion, and other compressible flow systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of spatially evolving supersonic turbulent shear layers.
Varied convective Mach number (Mc) and velocity parameter (λ) to isolate compressibility and advection effects.
Derived self-similar forms of continuity, momentum, and energy equations and an approximate cross-stream velocity relation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports collapse of normalized velocity and turbulence profiles in the self-similar region, linear growth of layer and momentum thickness, and agreement between the derived cross-stream velocity model and DNS results.
watch_item: The self-similar scalings and entrainment expression are derived and validated from DNS in a specific supersonic shear-layer setting, so extrapolation to other geometries, Reynolds numbers, or strongly non-equilibrium flows should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Compressibility and Velocity Parameter Effects on Spatially Evolving Supersonic Turbulent Shear Layers
